newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes stable in quiet market, Masila firm.
newsitem.headline: Crudes stable in quiet market, Masila firm.

text.p: Crude oil prices were steady in the early Asian market on Tuesday after suffering losses in overnight futures markets, traders said.
In the wet market, July Masila traded at firm levels, they said.
July Brent closed at $17.54 a barrel on London's IPE on Monday, the yearly spot low on the continuation chart, while in New York, July crude futures on NYMEX settled at $18.68, near the day's low.
In Tokyo at midday, July cash Brent was notionally assessed at $17.65/17.75.
In Brent/Dubai spreads, August was notionally assessed at 60/70 cents and September at 80/90 cents.
July/August Brent was notionally assessed at minus 30/minus 29 cents and August/September Brent at minus 21/minus 18 cents.
In the physical market, there were reports that several July Masila cargoes had recently been traded at premiums to the official selling price.

A South Korean trader appears to have sold 750,000 barrels to a trader at a premium of 10 cents above the official selling price, traders said. The same cargo was believed resold to a U.S. major at Dubai quotes plus 50 cents, they said.
Traders also said that one or two cargoes of July Masila had been sold from a trader to Thailand at OSP plus 10 cents.
There was also a vague report that the same trader had sold a cargo of the Yemeni crude to Brazil.
In other Gulf crudes, July Oman continued to look weak pressured by an absence of firm requirements for the two to three cargoes believed still available.
Oman was last reported traded at OSP minus 30 cents, and some traders said indications could fall further.
